corrected_claims: Replaced the false attribution of the Betti-number formula to Dolbeault theory for arbitrary compact complex manifolds by projective analytification being compact Kahler and Hodge decomposition, and stated the comparison of algebraic and holomorphic differential forms.
Descended radicality and equality of embedded reduced subspaces through the faithfully flat analytic local rings in Chow's theorem.
Reduced the Chow-lemma alteration explicitly, proved it projective, and used the sealed image-closure result plus uniqueness of reduced analytic structure on a closed analytic set.
Used the sealed algebraic-graph regularity proposition for algebraization of holomorphic maps and the compactness criterion for properness in the uniqueness corollary.
Restricted the GL_n stalk argument to closed points, descended finite projectivity, used freeness over a local ring, and globalized through the Jacobson property.
Restored the omitted second remark after Proposition 18 and the open bijectivity boundary attached to Proposition 20.

conclusion.recommendation: Append the candidate after the completed proofs of GAGA Theorems 1-3 and before the unique terminal input of the chapter list; then build, render, scan, and project all seventeen decisions in one no-overwrite mapping successor.

explicit_external_inputs: Compatibility of algebraic Kahler differentials with holomorphic differential forms on smooth analytifications.
Projective analytifications are compact Kahler and satisfy Hodge decomposition; the Betti-number formula is not asserted for arbitrary compact complex manifolds.
Compatibility of analytification with finite limits, graphs, proper images, and associated bundles.
The elementary analytic fact that a compact subset of a Hausdorff compactification is closed.
A reduced closed analytic subspace is determined by its underlying closed analytic set.
The extension theorem for embeddings of fields algebraic over Q into C.
Rosenlicht's rational-section theorem and rational symplectic Gram-Schmidt occur only in the examples remark and are not used by the comparison propositions.

projected_mapping_transaction.rationale: The application section defines conjugation and proves invariance of Betti numbers via flat base change, GAGA cohomology, and Dolbeault.
Exact modern scheme-theoretic form of Proposition 12 with all analytic input named.
The number-field embedding corollary follows from conjugation by an automorphism of C.
The historical non-isomorphism observation and homeomorphism question are preserved and isolated from the proof.
The Chow and algebraicity subsection assembles Propositions 13-15 and their corollary.
The candidate proves the source theorem for every projective algebraic variety, not only projective space; a coherent analytic ideal is algebraized by essential surjectivity and full faithfulness.
Compact analytic subspaces are reduced to projective Chow by compactification and Chow's lemma.
The graph of a holomorphic map from a proper variety is compact analytic and hence algebraic.
An analytic isomorphism between proper algebraizations and its inverse are regular.
The algebraic and analytic H1 pointed sets and the analytification map are defined using torsors.
An analytic bundle isomorphism is a holomorphic section of an algebraic Isom bundle and hence regular.
Additive torsors are H1 of the structure sheaf and are compared by GAGA cohomology.
GL_n torsors are vector bundles; coherent essential surjectivity plus faithfully flat descent recovers local freeness.
The Picard consequence and historical Kodaira-Spencer formulation are retained.
A reduction of an algebraic extended bundle is a section of the associated G/H-bundle and algebraizes by regularity.
GL_n algebraization and the reduction proposition prove bijectivity; Serre's examples are recorded separately.
Condition (R) is stated as the existence of a rational section of GL_n to GL_n/G.
